standard.title: Apply skills to communicate meaning
standard.description: apply technical and expressive skills and/or genre- or style-specific techniques to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use technical and expressive skills in own dance works (AC9ADA6C02). They have not yet applied skills with a clear rationale for how each contributes to communicating specific ideas, perspectives or meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply technical and expressive skills deliberately to communicate intended ideas, perspectives and meaning, using feedback to refine their application.

nodes.label: Applying technical skills to intensify communication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply specific technical skills to intensify the communication of mood, atmosphere or meaning in a dance
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least one technical skill (e.g. balance, strength, coordination) with a specific communicative purpose; explain how the skill contributes to the mood or meaning communicated
nodes.typical_width: Apply a range of technical skills across a dance to communicate choreographic intent; explain how each technical choice intensifies or clarifies the intended communication
wider: Investigate how mastery of a specific technical skill (e.g. controlled stillness, sustained movement quality) changes what a dance communicates — experiment with developing that skill to expressive purpose
Apply strength, balance and coordination simultaneously — evaluate the challenge of coordinating multiple technical demands while maintaining expressive clarity
Experiment with applying style-specific techniques from a dance genre that uses those techniques with different communicative purposes than own familiar style

response_modes.reason: Students commonly apply technical skills for their own sake — demonstrating what they can do — without connecting technical choices to communicative intent. Scaffolding the reasoning (what am I trying to communicate, which technical quality serves that, how does this skill intensify the intended effect?) builds the habit of purposeful technical application.

success_criteria: Applies at least one technical skill with a specific communicative purpose
Explains how the skill contributes to mood or meaning
Technical choices are connected to intent — not just demonstrations of ability

nodes.label: Using feedback to refine expressive and technical application
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use feedback to evaluate and refine how technical and expressive skills are communicating choreographic intent
nodes.minimum_width: Respond to at least one piece of feedback about technical or expressive skill application; document what changed and why
nodes.typical_width: Use feedback from peers and teachers to evaluate clarity of movement, projection, focus and musicality; refine technical and expressive application; document decisions using dance terminology
wider: Use Viewpoints questions alongside peer feedback to evaluate whether movement choices are communicating what is intended — 'What did you think the dance expressed?'
Use video to evaluate and refine spatial placement or articulation — compare video observation with own proprioceptive sense of the movement
Develop criteria for evaluating own technical and expressive application — articulate what 'clear communication' looks like across multiple technical and expressive dimensions

response_modes.reason: Using feedback to refine technical and expressive application requires sustained cycles of performing, receiving feedback, adjusting and performing again. The refinement habit develops through iteration, not through exposure to more feedback types or dance contexts.

success_criteria: Responds to at least one piece of feedback with a documented change
Explains what the feedback revealed about the technical or expressive application
Refinement is specific and connected to communicative intent

nodes.label: Integrated application of skills across a complete dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply technical and expressive skills consistently across a complete dance to communicate intended ideas, perspectives or meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Perform or present a dance that demonstrates at least two deliberate technical and expressive skill applications connected to intended meaning
nodes.typical_width: Perform or present a dance demonstrating consistent and deliberate application of technical and expressive skills across the whole work; evaluate whether the application successfully communicates the intended meaning
wider: Apply genre- or style-specific techniques with sufficient mastery that they carry the expressive content of the style — evaluate whether technique has moved from imitation to genuine stylistic expression
Perform the same dance material with deliberately different technical and expressive choices — evaluate how the changes alter what the dance communicates
Reflect on the relationship between technical mastery and expressive freedom — evaluate how technical development has expanded rather than constrained expressive possibilities

response_modes.reason: This node integrates purposeful technical application (Node 1), feedback-driven refinement (Node 2), and material developed through AC9ADA8C01 into a complete performed work. The coordination of technical and expressive skills across a whole dance is the learning — students who can apply skills in isolation but cannot sustain them across a complete work have not met the standard.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two deliberate technical and expressive applications in a complete dance
Applications are connected to intended meaning — not just demonstrations of skill
Can evaluate whether the application communicated the intended ideas
